```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md; ranking from your partner's words, 2026-11-06 ("rank them in the order you listed"). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace with four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a chosen range, downloaded and kept | §2.1, §4.2, R1 | A | 1 | Requests: about 2 per quarter (listing plus file), so minutes at 3 req/s; about 135 quarters if the range starts in 1993 (arithmetic from the full-index layout). Bytes per quarter measured by Stage 1. |
| O2 | New daily indexes picked up every day, with catch-up after missed runs | §2.1, §4.2, R2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year, so requests are negligible at 3 req/s. Bytes per day measured by Stage 3. |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, built from the downloaded indexes | §4.4–§4.6, R3 | A | 3 | Parse time and peak memory per quarter measured by Stage 1. |
| O4 | The pipelines running on Azure: ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor | §4.1, §4.9, R4 | A | 4 | Azure spend measured by Stage 7 and Stage 9. It cannot be estimated before resource sizes are chosen (§4.8). |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs share one downloader, parser and publisher | §4.1, R5 | A | 5 | Not material |
| O6 | Original index bytes kept, so a parser change rebuilds output with no new download | §4.3, §4.5, R6 | A | 6 | Storage is raw volume times the number of changed snapshots kept (content-addressed). Raw volume comes from Stage 1. |
| O7 | A weekly re-check of quarterly indexes that records additions and changed fields | §4.2, §4.4, R7 | A | 7 | About 1 request per supported quarter each week (§4.8 schedule). |
| O8 | All SEC traffic goes through one shared request budget | §4.3, R8 | A | 8 | Not material |
| O9 | Readers find each quarter's current data through one versioned pointer | §4.5, §4.6, R9 | A | 9 | Not material |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only after an approval tied to the source hash | §4.4, R10 | A | 10 | Your partner's time, one approval per withdrawing closed quarter. Frequency is unknown until Stage 5 runs. |
| O11 | Stated starting defaults for schedules, retries and request rate, changed only by config review | §4.8, R11 | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

- The repository has three scaffold packages that the spec does not name: `sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download` and `sec-edgar-index-ingest`. The spec puts all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (§4.9). Which package owns which code is settled in Stage 1's brainstorming. It does not block the partition.

## Stages

Order follows the ranking for O1 and O3, which make up the core. It diverges after that, by dependency:
- O6 comes before O2, because daily catch-up and pending-source revisits need durable source state (§4.2).
- O9 comes before O7 and O10, because reconciliation compares against the active generation (§4.4).
- O4 comes before O8, because the shared lease is Storage-backed (§4.3).
- Production operation comes last (§7, Phase 2).

- [ ] Stage 1: Core — one real quarter to canonical Parquet
      Objective: Download one real archived quarterly master index and turn it into canonical filing-index rows on a local machine.
      Outcomes: O1 (a range of one quarter), O3
      Consumes: nothing. Needs your partner's SEC User-Agent identity (§4.8) and the choice of quarter.
      Produces: a downloader (identifying User-Agent, at most 3 req/s) and a parser emitting the `sec-index-v1` row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the quarter's original bytes are on disk with their SHA-256. O3 — a Parquet file of that quarter's rows passes the §4.5 row contract with unique `(cik, archive_path)` keys. Cost — the findings file records bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and request count of the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest and content-addressed raw paths (Stage 2); daily indexes (Stage 3); quarter generations and active pointer (Stage 4); shared request budget, retry policy and validated configuration (Stage 8); Azure resources (Stage 7); golden fixtures across the backfill range, alerts, runbooks and triggers (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Source manifest and replay
      Objective: Keep raw snapshots content-addressed and track source, snapshot and processing states, so stored bytes can be replayed.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader and parser
      Produces: the source manifest (§4.5 records Source, Snapshot, Workset binding, Processing and Attempt); `downloaded -> transformed -> published` states; immutable worksets (§4.1)
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change rebuilds observation output from stored raw bytes with zero SEC requests, and unchanged hash plus versions is a no-op (§6 Replay tests pass).
      Leaves out: Table Storage and ADLS backing (Stage 7); quarter publication (Stage 4)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Daily ingestion and shared commands
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily indexes, with catch-up, through the same commands as backfill.
      Outcomes: O2, O5
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader and parser; Stage 2 source manifest
      Produces: `index.json` discovery for full-index and daily-index; `discover`, `collect` and `transform` commands shared by backfill and daily runs (§4.1); overlap deduplication (§4.4 Identity, Open quarter)
      Exit: O2 — one real published daily index ingests; §6 Discovery and coverage tests pass, including an outage across quarters and a failed listing that does not advance the boundary. O5 — backfill and daily runs call the same downloader and parser, shown by a test.
      Leaves out: daily trigger and catch-up from the real handoff date (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditional active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2 source manifest; Stage 3 shared commands
      Produces: the `publish` command; generations with manifest, change report and pointer (§4.5, §4.6)
      Exit: O9 — readers resolve data only through the pointer; §6 Publication crash-injection and competing-publisher tests pass.
      Leaves out: Table Storage conditional writes (Stage 7); withdrawal gate (Stage 6)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Quarterly reconciliation
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes and publish additions and field updates through the shared path.
      Outcomes: O7
      Consumes: Stage 4 publication; Stage 3 shared commands
      Produces: reconciliation runs on the shared commands; change records (§4.4 Changes)
      Exit: O7 — §6 Reconciliation tests for additions, field updates and open-quarter absence pass, and reconciliation uses the same downloader, parser and publisher as backfill.
      Leaves out: withdrawals (Stage 6); weekly trigger (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Withdrawal approval gate
      Objective: Stage closed-quarter replacements that remove keys until a hash-bound approval is given.
      Outcomes: O10
      Consumes: Stage 5 reconciliation; Stage 4 publication
      Produces: `awaiting_approval` candidates; withdrawal approval records (§4.5)
      Exit: O10 — §6 Reconciliation tests for hash-bound approval, non-reusable approval and stale daily replay pass.
      Leaves out: approval runbook (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment
      Objective: Run the shared commands on Azure resources under managed identities, with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 2–6 contracts; the ADR accepted (spec §7, step 1)
      Produces: infrastructure under version control (§4.9); ADF start-and-poll of Container Apps Jobs; ADLS and Table Storage backing for the source manifest and pointers; log delivery
      Exit: O4 — §6 Orchestration tests and the isolated-resource integration tests pass (spec §7, step 3), and every trigger is disabled.
      Leaves out: shared request budget (Stage 8); live smoke test, alerts, runbooks and triggers (Stage 9)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Shared request budget and configuration
      Objective: Put every SEC request behind one Storage-backed lease, the bounded retry policy and validated configuration.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 7 Azure Storage; Stage 3 and Stage 5 collectors
      Produces: the collector lease (§4.3); the retry and timeout policy; typed configuration with §4.8 defaults and §5 Configuration refusals
      Exit: O8 — §6 Access tests pass (concurrent collectors, lease takeover, Retry-After, halt on 403). O11 — invalid configuration is refused before external I/O, and the defaults match §4.8.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 9: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Smoke-test, backfill, catch up and enable triggers per spec §7 steps 4–9.
      Outcomes: O1 (full range), O2 (scheduled), O4 (operating)
      Consumes: Stages 1–8
      Produces: golden fixtures across the backfill range (§4.6); alerts (§4.7); runbooks (§8); release record; enabled triggers
      Exit: O1 — every requested quarter is published, or the incomplete range is recorded. O2 — observed scheduled daily runs match their reports. O4 — rollback and approval have been rehearsed, and the release record names the image, the configuration and the active generations.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, and writing-plans copies it verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

With every stage ticked, run the gap rubric over O1–O11. Each verdict needs evidence: a path:line or a test name, plus the stage plan that built it. A stage stamp alone is not evidence. Every spec requirement, R1–R11, is cited by some outcome's Spec cell, so there is no uncited requirement to add. Each unmet outcome exits one of two ways: a new stage, or deferral with a written reason.
```
